title: Completed scalars on an annihilated tower limit
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal, B its I-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and T an inverse system of A-modules indexed by natural numbers [def-weil-inverse-system], where index n denotes positive level n+1. Suppose I^(n+1)T_n=0 for every n. There exist a B-module N and an A-linear isomorphism e from its restriction to A to the categorical limit of T such that, whenever r in B has residue represented by a in A at level n+1, the nth projection of e(r x) is a times the nth projection of e(x). No finiteness or surjectivity hypothesis is assumed. The limit cone and scalar equation determine this pair up to a unique B-linear isomorphism respecting e.

source.place: Lemma 087W, proof, definition of M = lim M_n as a completed module

proof.text: Annihilation makes the scalar endomorphism A -> End_A(T_n) kill I^(n+1), so factor it through A/I^(n+1). Compose with the residue of the completion to obtain d_n: B -> End_A(T_n).

The maps d_n(r) commute with transitions. Represent r by a Cauchy sequence, so that at level n its action is multiplication by the nth representative. Representatives at comparable indices differ by an element of the smaller ideal power, which kills the smaller term. The universal property of the A-module limit lifts these coordinate endomorphisms to v(r).

Joint injectivity of the limit projections proves that v preserves addition, multiplication, zero and one. Thus v is a ring homomorphism into End_A(lim T); restrict the natural endomorphism-module action along it. For a scalar from A, the residue equation proves that this action recovers the original A-action. The identity on underlying elements is therefore the required restricted A-linear isomorphism e. The coordinate formula gives the assertion; joint injectivity also proves uniqueness.

lean.statement:
theorem adicTower_completedScalarLimit (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (T : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A)
    (hT : ∀ n : ℕ, I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A (T.obj (op n))) = ⊥) :
    ∃ N : ModuleCat.{u} (AdicCompletion I A),
    ∃ e : (restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).obj N ≅ limit T,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : AdicCompletion I A) (a : A) (x : N),
      AdicCompletion.evalₐ I (n + 1) r = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1)) a →
      (e.hom ≫ limit.π T (op n)) (r • x) =
        a • (e.hom ≫ limit.π T (op n)) x
